The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both the counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the Act'), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 05.04.2018.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that on 05.04.2018 at about 8:45 p.m., petitioner was proceeding on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-32-ER-6096 (for short 'motorcycle') as a pillion rider from his house to railway station.
His elder brother Sharathkumar was riding the same.

Near Shahabad ring road of Kalaburagi, a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-32-B-2386 ('offending vehicle' for short), being driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came and dashed against motorcycle.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment, petitioner is not completely cured.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.

6. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying that the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
Respondent No.2 further pleaded that since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, it is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the appeal.
7. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
8. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 21.
Respondent No.2 has not led any evidence.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.11,55,329/- and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same with interest at 6% pa as detailed below:

Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

13. Heard arguments and perused the records.
14.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.
15. Based on the SSLC marks card and other documents, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the petitioner as 23 years and appropriate multiplier as 18.

In the absence of proof of exact income,
having regard to the fact that accident is of the year 2018, the Tribunal has rightly taken his notional Chandrakanth vs Ashok And Anr on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162834157/

sentences.text: However, looking to the nature of injuries suffered, period of treatment, the disability ought to have been taken at 20% instead of 15%.

With these components, the loss of income due to disability is at Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 18 x 20% = Rs.5,07,600/- as against Rs.3,80,700/-
granted by the Tribunal.
16. Based on medical bills, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.4,14,129/- under the head medical expenses is correct.

Taking into consideration the nature of injuries suffered, period of treatment and the disability sustained, at the rate of Rs.11,750/- for a period of six months the Tribunal has correctly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.70,500/- under the head laid up period and Rs.50,000/- under the head attendant charges; Rs.40,000/- under the head pain & suffering and Rs.1,00,000/- under the head loss of amentias and Rs.1,00,000/- under the head future medical expenses.

17. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.12,82,229/- as against Rss.11,55,329/- granted by the Tribunal, together with interest at 6% p.a. (except on future medical expenses) as detailed below:

19. To this extent, the appeal deserves to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.12,82,229/- as against Rss.11,55,329/- granted by the Tribunal, together with interest at 6% p.a. (except on future medical expenses)
(iii) Respondent No.1/insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
 (Minus the compensation already  paid/deposited).
 (iv) Vide order dated 09.01.2023, the petitioner is not entitled to interest for delay of 241 days on the enhanced compensation.
(v) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
